info.name: Vuelto API
info.description:
Complete API surface of the Vuelto app (rename per app — see docs/REBRANDING.md).

**Setup**
1. Import `vuelto.local.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Start the stack: `docker compose up -d` (Postgres + Mailpit) and the API (`dotnet run --project src/Api --launch-profile https`).
3. SMTP must point at **Mailpit** (`localhost:1025`) for the OTP auto-fetch to work — if your `.env` overrides SMTP to a real provider, switch it back for API testing.

**Sign-in flow (folder 1):** `OTP — send` → `OTP — fetch code from Mailpit` (delivery is async; wait ~2–5 s after send) → `OTP — verify`. Tokens are stored in the environment and every request in the collection authenticates with them automatically. Auth requests send `X-Native-Client: true`, selecting the body token transport (no cookies needed in Postman); the refresh token rotates on every `Refresh` call.

**MFA:** if the account has MFA enabled, `OTP — verify` stores a `mfaChallenge` instead of tokens — run `MFA — verify (step-up)` with a TOTP or recovery code.

**Admin folder** needs the signed-in user's email in `Admin__StaffEmails__0` (API restart required). **Public API / Webhooks folders** are config-gated default-off (`PublicApi__Enabled=true`, `Webhooks__Enabled=true`).

request.description: Rate-limited 5/min per IP (429 after — QA-AUTH-11). Email delivery is async (outbox): wait a few seconds before fetching the code.

item.name: OTP — fetch code from Mailpit (local envs only)

request.description: Reads the newest Mailpit message and extracts the 6-digit OTP into {{otpCode}}. Only works in environments with a mailpitUrl (local). On hosted envs (staging/prod) email goes to REAL inboxes — read the code there and set {{otpCode}} manually (or paste it straight into 'OTP — verify').

exec: console.warn('This environment has no Mailpit (hosted env — real email). Read the OTP from your inbox and set {{otpCode}} manually.');
if (!msgs.length) { console.warn('Mailpit is empty — send the OTP first; delivery is async (wait ~2-5s).'); }
else console.warn('No 6-digit code in the newest email — is it the OTP email?');

header.description: Body token transport — refresh_token returned in JSON instead of a cookie (Postman-friendly).

request.description: Stores accessToken/refreshToken on success. If the account has MFA enabled, stores mfaChallenge instead — run 'MFA — verify (step-up)' next. 401 invalid_code = wrong/expired; 401 too_many_attempts = cumulative lockout (QA-AUTH-04); 429 = throttle.

exec: console.log('MFA required — challenge stored. Run: MFA — verify (step-up).');

request.description: Completes sign-in for an MFA-enabled account. Accepts a 6-digit TOTP or a single-use recovery code (case/hyphen/space-insensitive). Challenge is single-use and short-lived (~5 min).

exec: if (json.access_token) { pm.environment.set('accessToken', json.access_token); if (json.refresh_token) pm.environment.set('refreshToken', json.refresh_token); console.log('Step-up complete — tokens stored.'); }

request.description: Rotates the refresh token (old one is revoked; replaying it revokes every session — reuse detection). The stored refreshToken is updated automatically.
The verify half is a browser redirect flow (GET /api/auth/magic-link/verify?token=&email= → 302 to the web app) — click the link from Mailpit in a browser; it isn't meaningful as a pure API call.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Full-page navigation: 302 to the provider's consent screen. {provider} = a configured provider from GET /api/auth/providers. No auth; errors land on the client's /auth-error.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The PROVIDER redirects here after consent (carries its code/state). Issues the session (refresh cookie) and 302s to the client. Never called by an API client directly.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The emailed magic-link URL. Single-use, hashed, time-limited token in the query; consumes it, sets the refresh cookie (or MFA step-up redirect), then 302s to the client.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Opened in the OS browser by MAUI clients (WebAuthenticator). Like /login/{provider} but the callback returns a deep link carrying a one-time code instead of a cookie.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Provider redirect for the native flow: issues a short-lived ONE-TIME CODE and 302s to the app's custom-scheme deep link. The code is redeemed via POST /api/auth/native/exchange.

Redeems the one-time code from the native callback deep link for tokens on the BODY transport (access + refresh token JSON; no cookie). 400/401 invalid_code on unknown/expired/replayed codes (single-use, 5-min TTL); {mfa_required, challenge} when the user has MFA enabled — step up via POST /api/auth/mfa/verify. Requires the X-Native-Client: true header.

en / es shipped. Drives UI + email language. Follows the user across devices: applied (with one reload on mismatch) on every sign-in, and a device-local login-page choice is adopted here automatically on sign-in when unset (PREFS-1, ADR-022). With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).

light / dark / system (THEME-1 + PREFS-1, ADR-022). All three are stored verbatim and follow the user across devices — "system" means follow the OS scheme; null in the DB means "never chose" (lets sign-in adopt a device-local choice). Lands in the JWT on the next refresh. Anything else → 400 unsupported_theme. With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).
Fail-closed: refuses to remove your last sign-in method (QA-SET-05). Link-start (POST /api/auth/link/{provider}) is a browser redirect flow.
GDPR erasure — IRREVERSIBLE. Owner-with-members → 400 (transfer first). Sole owner → 409 until confirm_dissolve=true (which also dissolves the household).

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Starts linking an additional OAuth provider to the signed-in account: responds with the provider redirect carrying a short-lived link token; completes at the callback with ?linked=… (or ?link_error=…) on the client's /settings. Requires the Bearer token.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Time-limited signed download URL minted by the export/file surfaces (FILES-2; the token IS the authorization — DataProtection-signed, tenant-scoped). Browser navigation; responds with Content-Disposition: attachment.
Returns the otpauth:// provisioning URI + Base32 secret (shown once). Add the secret to an authenticator app, then Confirm.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('mfaSecret', json.secret); console.log('Secret (add to authenticator):', json.secret); console.log(json.provisioning_uri); }

request.description: Enables MFA and returns the 10 one-time recovery codes (xxxxx-xxxxx) — logged to console, shown ONCE.

exec: if (codes) console.log('RECOVERY CODES (save now, shown once):', codes.join(', '));

request.description: Returns the raw token ONCE (also emailed). 402 = seat quota reached (QA-HH-14). 409 = already a member.

Sign in as the invitee first (re-run folder 1 with the invitee email) — accept joins the CALLER to the inviting household. Errors: 400 invitation_invalid/must_transfer_first/would_abandon_data, 409 already_member, 402 seat_limit_reached when the household downgraded below its reserved seats (BILLING-9 — the token stays pending and works again after an upgrade).
Roles: member | admin (owner is transferred, never assigned). Owner-only.
Owner-only; you become a member afterwards.
Member: leaves + re-homes to a fresh solo household. Owner with members: refused (transfer first). Sole owner: needs confirm_dissolve=true (dissolves).
GDPR export. Returns a signed, time-limited download URL (stored as {{exportDownloadUrl}} — use 'Files — download export'). Metered per plan (402 when the monthly quota is spent).

exec: if (url) { pm.environment.set('exportDownloadUrl', url.startsWith('http') ? url : pm.environment.get('baseUrl') + url); console.log('exportDownloadUrl stored'); }

request.description: The signed URL from the export (GET /api/files/{token}); no bearer needed — the token IS the auth, and it expires.

Clears ALL of the caller's notifications. The scope is REQUIRED (v3 LB-UI-10): read=false = all, read=true = only read; omitting ?read is a 400 (scope_required), so delete-all can never be hit by a dropped param.
Plan, status, seats — owner-only (403 otherwise).
Returns the provider checkout URL (fake provider locally: billing.test/... — won't load, by design).

header.description: The FAKE provider accepts the literal 'valid' (dev only). Real Stripe uses stripe CLI / real signatures.

request.description: Upgrades {{tenantId}} to pro/active as if checkout completed (QA-BILL upgrade loop). Requires the FAKE provider (dev default) — on an environment wired to real Stripe (test mode), this returns 400 invalid signature by design; use `stripe trigger` there instead. Run 'Get household' first to populate {{tenantId}}. Re-sending the same EventId is deduped (inbox); an older OccurredAt than the last applied event is ignored.

item.name: 8 · Admin (platform staff)
item.description: Requires the signed-in user's email in Admin__StaffEmails__0 (repo .env) + API restart. Non-staff → 403 everywhere except 'Am I staff'. An impersonation token ({{impersonationToken}} as bearer) → 403 impersonation_not_allowed on every staff action, and 'Am I staff' reports false — staff powers never transit a sign-in-as session (v3 ADM-2).

exec: if (list.length) { pm.environment.set('adminTenantId', list[0].id); console.log('adminTenantId =', list[0].id, '(' + list[0].name + ')'); }

item.name: Announce to tenant (all members or user_ids subset)

request.description: user_ids: null/omitted = every member; a NON-empty list = just those (intersected with the roster); an explicitly-empty [] = NO ONE (v3 LB-ADM-2). Audited in-tenant.
Queued (202) — the outbox dispatcher fans out a few seconds later. ADR-021.

Simulates a completed checkout (active, never lapses, no provider ids). 409 = tenant has a LIVE Stripe subscription — keyed on liveness (status ≠ canceled), so a churned/canceled tenant is comp-able even though it kept its Stripe id (ADR-006/021, v3 ADM-5).
Deletes the projection (absence ⇒ Free). Idempotent. 409 = LIVE provider subscription (status ≠ canceled); a canceled-but-lingering projection is cleaned up, not blocked (v3 ADM-5).

Stores {{impersonationToken}} (does NOT overwrite your session). To act as the target, temporarily set a request's bearer to {{impersonationToken}}. ~15 min, non-refreshable, audited in the target's tenant.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { pm.environment.set('impersonationToken', pm.response.json().access_token); console.log('impersonationToken stored (expires_in:', pm.response.json().expires_in + 's)'); }

request.description: Staff recovery path (ADR-021 addendum): wipes the user's TOTP secret + recovery codes WITHOUT a code — verify their identity out-of-band first. Also REVOKES the target's refresh tokens/sessions (v3 ADM-7 — compromise recovery). Audited in the target's tenant (admin.mfa.reset) and the user is notified (in-app + email). 204 also when the user had no MFA (idempotent no-op).

item.name: 9 · Public API & keys (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set PublicApi__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Key management is owner-only JWT; /api/public/* authenticates with the key itself.

request.description: Raw pk_ key returned ONCE — stored as {{apiKey}}.

exec: if (json.key) { pm.environment.set('apiKey', json.key); console.log('apiKey stored (shown once):', json.prefix + '…'); }

request.description: Key → tenant-scoped principal. Also accepts Authorization: Bearer pk_… . Per-key rate limit: 60/min → 429.

item.name: 10 · Outbound webhooks (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set Webhooks__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Owner-only. Target URLs must be public-routable (SSRF guard blocks localhost/private ranges) — use https://webhook.site or similar.

request.description: Signing secret (whsec_…) returned ONCE — stored as {{webhookSecret}}. 400 = SSRF guard rejected the URL.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('webhookSecret', json.secret); console.log('webhookSecret stored (shown once)'); }

request.description: Synchronously POSTs a signed test 'ping' and returns { delivered, status_code } (or { delivered:false, error:'delivery_failed' } on a transport error). Records a WebhookDelivery row for the attempt (success and failure), so the Delivery log is populated immediately — run it, then the Delivery log request.

Recent delivery attempts for this subscription (newest first, tenant-scoped): each row has success, status_code, error, event_id. Populated by Send test event (sync) and by published/replayed events (async via the outbox). Captures the newest row's id into {{deliveryId}} for Replay.

Re-enqueues the exact stored payload of {{deliveryId}} (same event id, so a receiver can dedup) → 202; delivered async via the outbox with retry/backoff, which logs its own attempt row. 404 for an unknown or other-tenant delivery id.

item.name: 11 · Budget settings
item.description: BUDGET-1 (app slice): the household's budget structure — week-start weekday, month anchor, and the two incomes' 4-week / 5-week defaults. One row per household, created on the first PUT; before that GET serves the defaults with is_default=true. Any member may read and save (no owner gate). Error codes: 400 invalid_request (message names the field), 401 without a token.

request.description: Returns the saved row, or the defaults (Thursday, last_weekday_prev, 0 USD × 2) flagged is_default=true when the household has never saved. Never writes.

Upserts the household's single row. week_start_weekday 0 (Sunday) … 6 (Saturday); month_anchor one of last_weekday_prev | first_weekday_current | first_of_month; amounts ≥ 0; currencies CRC or USD (case-insensitive, stored upper). 400 invalid_request otherwise; nothing is written on a 400.
Weekday 9 → 400 invalid_request; the message names week_start_weekday.

item.name: 12 · Catalog (categories + banks)
item.description: CATALOG-1/2 (app slice P2, ADR-V008): the household's two soft-delete name catalogs. One behaviour, two prefixes: /api/categories and /api/banks. Any member may read and edit. No DELETE — deactivate instead; inactive names keep labelling history.

request.description: Active by default; include_inactive=true for the management screen. The FIRST read for a household seeds the default categories in the caller's JWT locale (once). Captures the first id into {{categoryId}}.

201 with the entry. Names are unique per household, case-insensitively: an active clash is 409 category_exists; an inactive clash is 409 category_exists_inactive with existing_id + existing_name (offer reactivation via PUT name=existing_name, is_active=true). Blank name → 400 invalid_request.
Same name, different case → 409 category_exists (or category_exists_inactive with existing_id + existing_name if it was deactivated).
Rename and/or flip is_active. Rename clash → 409 category_exists; unknown or another household's id → 404 (uniform, ADR-V008).
Active by default; include_inactive=true for the management screen. The FIRST read for a household seeds the default banks in the caller's JWT locale (once). Captures the first id into {{bankId}}.

201 with the entry. Names are unique per household, case-insensitively: an active clash is 409 bank_exists; an inactive clash is 409 bank_exists_inactive with existing_id + existing_name (offer reactivation via PUT name=existing_name, is_active=true). Blank name → 400 invalid_request.
Same name, different case → 409 bank_exists (or bank_exists_inactive with existing_id + existing_name if it was deactivated).
Rename and/or flip is_active. Rename clash → 409 bank_exists; unknown or another household's id → 404 (uniform, ADR-V008).

item.name: 13 · Exchange rate
item.description: FX-1 (app slice P3, ADR-V006): the resolved USD→CRC rate and where it came from. Chain: live provider quote (cached 1 h counts as live) → stale cache flagged as of its fetch time → the household's most recent transaction rate → 503 exchange_rate_unavailable. Never a fabricated rate. Any member may read. Provider key: ExchangeRate__ApiKey in .env (unset ⇒ the chain starts at the cache).

request.description: 200 { rate, source: live | cache | transaction, as_of } — or 503 { error: exchange_rate_unavailable, message } when the whole chain is empty (no key / provider down, nothing cached, no transactions yet). Repeat within the hour: same as_of (cached, no provider call). 401 without a token.

exec: pm.test("200 with a rate, or the honest 503", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 503]));

item.name: 14 · Envelopes
item.description: ENV-1 (app slice P4, ADR-V007/V008): the household's savings envelopes — name, annual_target_crc / annual_target_usd (either may be 0), reminder_cadence monthly | five_week_months, soft delete. Same catalog rules as categories/banks: unique per household case-insensitively, 409 envelope_exists (active) or envelope_exists_inactive + existing_id + existing_name (offer Reactivate via PUT name=existing_name, is_active=true), uniform 404 for another household's id. Never seeded. Any member may read and edit.

request.description: Active by default; include_inactive=true for the management screen. A fresh household gets []. Captures the first id into {{envelopeId}}.
201 with the envelope (cadence normalized to lower-case, name trimmed). Re-run → 409 envelope_exists; after deactivating it → 409 envelope_exists_inactive + existing_id + existing_name.
400 invalid_request; the message names the field (reminder_cadence must be monthly or five_week_months). Also 400: blank name, name over 100 characters, a negative target.

200 with the envelope. is_active=false deactivates (soft delete — no DELETE route); is_active=true reactivates. Renaming onto another envelope's name → 409 envelope_exists; an id from another household → 404.

item.name: 15 · Months
item.description: LEDGER-1 (app slice P5a, ADR-V005): pay-cycle budget months. There is NO create route — a month appears when the first transaction lands in its anchor window (weeks materialized, income snapshotted from Budget settings) and leaves with its last transaction. Resolve answers for any date without writing. Any member may read and edit income.

request.description: Newest first. A fresh household gets []. Captures the first id into {{monthId}}.

Which budget month a date belongs to — by anchor window, not calendar month (2026-05-30 → June under the default anchor). An uncovered date answers the month that WOULD be created with is_new=true and month_id=null; nothing is written. Missing date → 400.

exec: pm.test("shape", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('is_new'); pm.expect(b.month_number).to.be.within(1, 12); });

request.description: The month with its materialized weeks (week_number, start_date, end_date). 404 not_found for another household's id or a month that left with its last transaction.

exec: pm.test("200 or 404 when no month yet", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

request.description: Both incomes stay editable after auto-creation (amount + currency each). 400 invalid_request for a negative amount or a currency other than CRC/USD; 404 for another household's id.

exec: pm.test("200 or 404 when no month yet", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

request.description: A negative amount → 400 invalid_request (message names the rule). Same for an unknown currency.
The month's rows newest first with category_name / bank_name resolved (inactive names still render — ADR-V008) and source (manual | email | refund_realization). 404 for an unknown month.

exec: pm.test("200 or 404 when no month yet", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

item.name: 16 · Transactions
item.description: LEDGER-2 (app slice P5a, ADR-V006/V007): money movement in both currencies at a frozen rate. POST validates everything, settles the rate (manual exchange_rate override wins, else the live → cache → last-transaction chain; nothing → 400 exchange_rate_unavailable), resolves or creates the month from transaction_date, derives amount_crc/amount_usd and freezes exchange_rate_used. PUT re-derives from the frozen rate (never sends a rate) and re-resolves the month on a date change; DELETE is hard and removes an emptied month. Rows with source != manual are read-only (400 derived_transaction). Uniform 404 for another household's id. Run 12 · Catalog first so {{categoryId}} and a bank exist. LEDGER-3: an unplanned_essential may carry refund_expected + refund_percentage (0 < p ≤ 100) — a derived Refund (percentage × the frozen amounts) is created/re-derived/removed with the transaction; the flag is ignored on other classes.

request.description: 201 with the row (amounts derived, rate frozen, source manual, month_id of the resolved-or-created month). Replace bank_id with an id from 12 · Catalog → List banks. Captures {{transactionId}} and {{monthId}}. Set transaction_type unplanned_essential + refund_expected true + refund_percentage (e.g. 30) to spawn an expected refund (see 17 · Refunds); the response echoes refund_expected / refund_percentage.

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set('transactionId', b.id); pm.environment.set('monthId', b.month_id);

request.description: 400 invalid_request; the message names the field (here: currency must be CRC or USD). Also 400: blank payee, amount ≤ 0, no date, unknown class/payment method, missing or unknown/inactive bank/category, exchange_rate ≤ 0, envelope rules (contribution needs an active envelope + bank_account; other classes must not carry one).
The row with both amounts and exchange_rate_used. 404 for another household's id.

200 with the row; amounts re-derived from the FROZEN exchange_rate_used (a rate in the body is ignored — there is no field). A changed transaction_date re-resolves the month (creating the target, deleting the emptied source). 400 derived_transaction for a non-manual row; 404 for another household's id. Set transaction_type unplanned_essential + refund_expected true + refund_percentage (e.g. 30) to spawn an expected refund (see 17 · Refunds); the response echoes refund_expected / refund_percentage.
204. Deleting a month's last transaction deletes the month and its weeks too (ADR-V005). 404 for an unknown or another household's id; 400 derived_transaction for a non-manual row.

item.name: 17 · Refunds
item.description: LEDGER-3 (app slice P5b, ADR-V007/V014): expected refunds derived from unplanned_essential transactions flagged refund_expected + refund_percentage (see 16 · Transactions). Amounts = percentage × the frozen amounts; the refund follows every edit and dies with its transaction. The ONLY directly editable field is status: received books a derived inflow transaction (same amounts, the source's frozen rate/bank/category, source refund_realization) and links it; pending removes the inflow. The flip is a conditional update — concurrent flips book exactly one inflow (loser: 409 refund_status_conflict). Uniform 404 for another household's id.

request.description: The month's expected refunds newest first: payee, transaction_date, percentage, amount_crc, amount_usd, status (pending | received), inflow_transaction_id (present ⇔ received). Captures the first id into {{refundId}}. 404 for an unknown month.

exec: pm.test("200 or 404 when no month yet", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));
if (pm.response.code === 200) { const items = pm.response.json(); if (Array.isArray(items) && items.length) pm.environment.set('refundId', items[0].id); }

request.description: received → 200 with inflow_transaction_id set and a derived inflow in the month's transactions (read-only there: 400 derived_transaction). pending → 200, inflow removed. Same status → 200 no-op. 400 invalid_request for any other status; 404 for another household's id; 409 refund_status_conflict when a concurrent flip won (reload and retry).

item.name: 18 · Expenses (fixed + variable)
item.description: EXPENSES-1 (app slice P6, ADR-V007/V008): the budget baseline — two ordered lists of single-currency lines under /api/expenses/fixed and /api/expenses/variable, identical behaviour. Each line: name (unique per list), budget_crc XOR budget_usd, payment_method, a REQUIRED active category that backs at most one active line across both lists, an optional active bank (null = Unassigned), sort_order owned by the order route. Soft delete with the 409 reactivation offer; never seeded; uniform 404. Any member may edit.

request.description: Active by default, ordered by sort_order; include_inactive=true for the management screen. Never seeded (a fresh household gets []). Captures the first id into {{fixedExpenseId}}.

201 with the line (sort_order appended). Single-currency: exactly one of budget_crc / budget_usd non-zero. category_id required, active, and backing NO other active line in EITHER list; bank_id optional (active). Names unique per list, case-insensitively: 409 expense_exists / expense_exists_inactive + existing_id + existing_name (offer Reactivate via PUT name=existing_name, is_active=true). Run 12 · Catalog first so {{categoryId}} exists.

Both budgets non-zero → 400 invalid_request ("exactly one of budget_crc or budget_usd…"). Also 400: blank name, unknown payment_method, missing/unknown/inactive/foreign category, unknown/inactive bank, negative budget, a category already backing another active line.

200 with the line. Every editable field changes (name, budgets, payment_method, category_id, bank_id — null clears it, is_active); sort_order is NEVER changed here (the order route owns it). 409 on a rename onto another line's name; 400 on a category that backs another active line; 404 for another household's id.
204. ordered_ids must be EXACTLY the active fixed lines (no missing, unknown, inactive or repeated id) → else 400 invalid_request; positions land atomically as sort_order 0..n.

exec: pm.test("204 or 400 when the set differs", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([204, 400]));

request.description: Active by default, ordered by sort_order; include_inactive=true for the management screen. Never seeded (a fresh household gets []). Captures the first id into {{variableExpenseId}}.

201 with the line (sort_order appended). Single-currency: exactly one of budget_crc / budget_usd non-zero. category_id required, active, and backing NO other active line in EITHER list; bank_id optional (active). Names unique per list, case-insensitively: 409 expense_exists / expense_exists_inactive + existing_id + existing_name (offer Reactivate via PUT name=existing_name, is_active=true). Run 12 · Catalog first so {{categoryId}} exists.

Both budgets non-zero → 400 invalid_request ("exactly one of budget_crc or budget_usd…"). Also 400: blank name, unknown payment_method, missing/unknown/inactive/foreign category, unknown/inactive bank, negative budget, a category already backing another active line.

200 with the line. Every editable field changes (name, budgets, payment_method, category_id, bank_id — null clears it, is_active); sort_order is NEVER changed here (the order route owns it). 409 on a rename onto another line's name; 400 on a category that backs another active line; 404 for another household's id.
204. ordered_ids must be EXACTLY the active variable lines (no missing, unknown, inactive or repeated id) → else 400 invalid_request; positions land atomically as sort_order 0..n.

exec: pm.test("204 or 400 when the set differs", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([204, 400]));

item.name: 19 · Dashboard
item.description: DASH-1 (app slice P7, ADR-V004/V006/V007): the month at a glance. GET /api/months/{id}/summary returns the month header (id, year, month_number, week_count, week1_start_date, last_day), the rate resolved through the chain (exchange_rate, rate_source live|cache|transaction, rate_as_of) and the summary — every figure a {crc, usd} pair rounded to 2 dp. Actuals sum each transaction's frozen amounts; projections (income conversion, budget display, pending_budgeted, remainder_for_debts) use the resolved rate. When nothing resolves: rate_unavailable true, exchange_rate and summary null (projections are blocked, never guessed). Uniform 404 for an unknown or foreign month. Run 15 · Months first so {{monthId}} exists.

request.description: 200 { month, exchange_rate, rate_source, rate_as_of, rate_unavailable, summary }. summary: income_primary/secondary/total, expenses_card/account/total/remainder, fixed_expenses[] + variable_expenses[] ({name, budget, actual}), other_spending[] ({category_name, actual} — expense-class spend in categories no active line backs, ₡ desc then name), weekly_budgeted[] + weekly_extraordinary[] ({week_number, start_date, end_date, total}), current_balance, remainder_for_debts, pending_budgeted, actual_remainder, unplanned_essential_total, refunds_total (pending only), envelope_reminders[] ({name, annual_target, contributed_this_month, remaining, cadence}), bank_method_breakdown[] ({bank_id (null = Unassigned, last), bank_name, payment_method, budget, actual}). 404 when the month is unknown or another household's.

exec: pm.test("rate or blocked", () => pm.expect(d.rate_unavailable ? d.summary === null : typeof d.exchange_rate === 'number').to.be.true);
const other = d.summary.other_spending.reduce((a, c) => a + c.actual.crc, 0);

request.description: Uniform 404 not_found for an unknown id — the same answer another household's month gets (no existence oracle).

item.name: 20 · Reports
item.description: REPORTS-1/2 (app slice P8, ADR-V004/V005/V006 + platform ADR-010): read-only reporting over the frozen transaction amounts. Category analysis groups the spending classes (budgeted / extraordinary / unplanned_essential — never inflow or envelope_contribution) by category; a single month also decorates budgeted entries with the catalog budget. The CSV export stores the file through IFileStorage and returns a 15-minute signed download_url (served anonymously by GET /api/files/{token}) — the same download affordance the household export uses, so web and MAUI share one path. Run 15 · Months first so {{monthId}} exists. Period: month_id (the month's anchor window — first week start to the LAST week's end date) OR from + to (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive), never both, never neither → 400 period_required / period_ambiguous / period_incomplete / period_invalid. Unknown or another household's month_id → uniform 404.

request.description: 200 { period {from, to}, single_month: true, budgeted[], extraordinary[], unplanned_essential[] }; each entry { category_id, category_name, total_crc, total_usd, budgeted_crc, budgeted_usd } — the budget fields are the sum of the active fixed + variable lines backing the category (null when none) and are present ONLY for a single month. Zero-spend categories are absent; sorted by name; names from the all-states catalog. Period: month_id (the month's anchor window — first week start to the LAST week's end date) OR from + to (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive), never both, never neither → 400 period_required / period_ambiguous / period_incomplete / period_invalid. Unknown or another household's month_id → uniform 404.
200 with single_month: false — budgeted_crc / budgeted_usd are null on every entry (a monthly budget does not multiply across arbitrary ranges).

exec: pm.test("range has no budgets", () => { pm.expect(r.single_month).to.be.false; r.budgeted.forEach(e => pm.expect(e.budgeted_crc).to.be.null); });

request.description: No month_id and no range → 400 period_required. Also: month_id + from → period_ambiguous; only from → period_incomplete; from > to or a non-ISO date → period_invalid.

200 { download_url, file_name "transactions-<today>.csv", row_count, period, expires_in_seconds 900 }. Optional filters: category_id, class (normalized). The CSV (RFC 4180, UTF-8, CRLF): date,payee,category,class,amount_crc,amount_usd,exchange_rate_used,payment_method,bank,source — amounts 2 dp without symbols, exchange_rate_used 4 dp, dates yyyy-MM-dd, rows date desc then created desc, header-only when nothing matches (never 404). Open download_url WITHOUT a token: the signed link is the authorization; it expires after 15 minutes (then 404). Captures the link into {{exportUrl}}. Period: month_id (the month's anchor window — first week start to the LAST week's end date) OR from + to (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive), never both, never neither → 400 period_required / period_ambiguous / period_incomplete / period_invalid. Unknown or another household's month_id → uniform 404.

item.name: 21 · Email inboxes
item.description: EMAIL-2/3 (app slice P9b, ADR-V002/V016): the caller's read-only inbox connections — USER-keyed (survive leaving a household; erased with the account). Created ONLY through the consent round-trip: GET authorize → the IdP → the anonymous GET callback (the signed 15-minute state is its authorization) → /email?connected=… Tokens are protected by the platform Data Protection key ring and never returned. One inbox per provider. Unknown or another user's id → uniform 404.

request.description: 200 [ { id, provider, account_email, status active|needs_reconsent, folders[], sender_filters[], subject_filters[], unread_only, ignore_cursor, import_from, polling_interval_minutes, last_polled_at, created_at } ] — never tokens. Captures the first id into {{emailConnectionId}}.

200 { authorization_url } — the read-only consent URL (gmail.readonly + openid email, access_type=offline, prompt=consent, login_hint = your email, a signed state). Open it in a browser; the IdP returns to GET …/callback, which creates the connection and redirects to /email. 400 provider_not_configured when Authentication:Google has no ClientId on this API; 400 invalid_provider for anything but microsoft|google.
400 invalid_provider.

The IdP redirect target — anonymous (no bearer). A missing/tampered/expired state, or error=…, creates nothing and redirects to {{clientUrl}}/email?email_error=consent_failed (already_connected when the provider is connected twice). Postman follows redirects by default; disable it in the request settings to see the 302 + Location.

exec: pm.test("redirected or followed to the client", () => pm.expect([302, 200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: 200 { sender_filters[] (verified BAC/BN From-addresses), subject_filters[] (the routing subject prefixes), banks[] { name, sender_filters, subject_filters } } — what the connect flow pre-seeds.
Always 400 use_consent_flow — tokens never arrive in a client body; only the consent callback creates connections.
200 with the connection (no tokens); 404 for an unknown or another user's id.
200 [ { id, name } ] — the account's real folders (Graph: subfolders as Inbox/Vouchers) or labels (Gmail), read live with the refresh-once rule; 409 needs_reconsent on a dead token; 404 unknown.

200 with the connection. folders[] (provider ids), sender_filters[] / subject_filters[] (≥ 1 total → else 400 filters_required), unread_only, ignore_cursor (fetch all unread regardless of date), import_from (lowering it pulls last_polled_at back for a backfill; raising it never advances the cursor), polling_interval_minutes 5…1440 (else 400 invalid_interval). 404 for another user's id.

{
  "folders": [],
  "sender_filters": [
    "notificacion@notificacionesbaccr.com",
    "bncontacto@bncr.fi.cr"
  ],
  "subject_filters": [
    "Notificación de transacción",
    "Voucher Digital",
    "BN Conectividad le informa"
  ],
  "unread_only": true,
  "ignore_cursor": false,
  "import_from": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z",

request.description: EMAIL-4: stage this inbox's matching mail immediately (read -> parse -> inert drafts in the owner's CURRENT household, deduped by fingerprint). 200 { staged, duplicates, unrecognized }; 409 needs_reconsent when the token is dead (the row is flagged); 404 for an unknown or another user's id. Mail is never marked read: a re-run reports the same emails under duplicates. The background email-poll job does the same on each connection's own interval.
204 — ingestion stops; already-imported transactions stay. 404 for an unknown or another user's id.

item.name: 22 · Review queue & merchant suggestions
item.description: EMAIL-5/6 (app slice P10b, ADR-V010). HOUSEHOLD-scoped. Merchant → category rules only ever SUGGEST on a staged draft (case-insensitive contains, longest pattern wins; one rule per merchant text per household). The review queue is the ONLY draft → transaction path: confirm books the transaction through the same create as manual entry (month auto-created, live rate frozen, source = email) and flips the draft with a conditional update in one transaction — a concurrent second confirm gets 409 not_pending and its transaction rolls back; discard is the same guarded flip. Foreign ids → uniform 404. Needs a category id in {{categoryId}} (run 12 · Categories first).

request.description: 200 [ { id, merchant_pattern, category_id, category_name, suggested_class } ] ordered by pattern. Captures the first id into {{merchantMappingId}}.

201 with the rule (pattern trimmed; suggested_class budgeted|extraordinary|unplanned_essential or null). 400 invalid_request (blank pattern, unknown class, missing/inactive/foreign category); 409 mapping_exists when the same merchant text exists in any casing. Captures {{merchantMappingId}}.
409 mapping_exists — 'automercado' clashes with 'AUTOMERCADO' (case-insensitive uniqueness per household).
200 with the rule; 400 invalid_request; 409 mapping_exists when the new text clashes with ANOTHER rule; 404 unknown/foreign.
204 — plain delete (a rule is copied onto drafts at staging, never referenced afterwards). 404 unknown/foreign.

200 [ { id, parsed_bank, merchant, amount, currency, date, bank_id, card_number, authorization, reference, transaction_type, missing_fields[], suggested_category_id, suggested_class, received_at } ] — pending drafts only, newest mail first. Captures the first id into {{pendingVoucherId}}.
200 { count } — what the header badge and the dashboard banner show.

200 { transaction_id, month_id, amount_crc, amount_usd, remembered } — books the transaction (source = email) through the ordinary create and flips the draft. category_id + transaction_class (budgeted|extraordinary|unplanned_essential) are required; payee / bank_id / payment_method / original_amount / currency / transaction_date override the parsed values (the UI opens only the blanks); remember_merchant creates a merchant rule (never overwrites). 400 invalid_request / exchange_rate_unavailable (nothing written, draft stays pending); 409 not_pending (already confirmed/discarded, or lost a concurrent confirm — its transaction rolled back); 404 unknown/foreign.
204 — the draft is discarded; the dedup tombstone stays so the same email never re-stages. 409 not_pending when a concurrent confirm/discard already actioned it; 404 unknown/foreign.
